## bijection_verdict
**PASS.** Notes (not KB defects):
- N1 (framework): GT step `verify_customer_identity` is not a tires-policy atom; runtime system background, out of KB scope.
- N7 (retired-surface scope, informational): the source replacement for "A set with any treadwear adjustment or workmanship replacement is past the trial" reads "For a trial refund this policy pays, **and only for such a refund**, …"; the hub carries "For a trial refund, …" and the retired-surface line says "no longer in force in that form; it is superseded by the current trial-refund basis", without stating that the old clause still governs any other return. The scoping phrase "For a trial refund" keeps the entailment for every return the tools can book (both request types run through this policy), so no permitted action or number changes.
- B1 (base, source-side): trial miles are "read at the store when the tires come off" (base, carried verbatim), while the confirm tool records "odometer reading the customer reports" and the usage charge reads the latest inspection odometer. Three odometers for one notion; here 2,492 (reported) and 2,360 (inspection) are both within 3,000, so no scored value moves.
- S3 (source-side, rule vs compute): bundle window lower bound exists only in compute (above).

## dependency_form
Hop T1 state-derived, not pre-solved. Titles are general subjects ("Satisfaction-Trial Return Confirmation", "Workmanship Replacement Posting"); no route, table or chain; the posting hub names only its own tool and the trial hub only its own.

**KB-EXPLICIT RED — class "computation document hints at a variation"** (every member across the product):
- **KB-E3** `trial_refund_amount_9a784ee4` (computation document, role baseline, of tires_ext_trial_refund), bullet 3: "**Days kept** — the calendar days from the install date to today." The baseline rule does not contain this quantity and the baseline formula never uses it ("the tire price paid plus the refunded installation part"); it is read only by the factors installation part, usage charge and truck-size restock (`trial_refund_installation_part`, `trial_usage_charge`, `truck_size_trial_restocking`, each of which defines days kept itself). A defined-but-unused, time-based quantity in the computation document signals that something in the refund varies with how long the set was kept, i.e. it pre-solves part of the factor search. Rendering-side (the source baseline is silent on days kept; the sentence comes from the policy's general rule).
- **S2 (source-side member, not a KB verdict)** `workmanship_share_amount_a5d1e557` (computation document of tires_ext_workmanship_share), "Miles run — that entry's odometer less the install odometer." The baseline formula never uses miles run (only proration_basis_method and maintained_set_discount do), but the sentence is part of the source baseline rule itself ("The miles run are that entry's odometer minus install_odometer."), which the KB must carry complete; reported as a source-side baseline item.
- Other computation documents checked (`treadwear_adjustment_credit_calculation`, `share_settlement_amount`, `replacement_ticket_balance`, `lapsed_order_refund_amount`): no unused quantity, no "unless/adjustments/elsewhere" wording.

**Class "factor document describes another policy's factor"** — KB-E1 and KB-E2 (recorded in 0.md). KB-E2's document belongs to tires_ext_share_settlement but its phrase "as the workmanship replacement was charged" describes this task's replacement_mounting_waiver factor; it is listed here for completeness and counted once, under task 0.

Verdict for task 1: **KB-EXPLICIT RED (KB-E3)**; semantics and solution unaffected (runtime PASS, bijection PASS).
